active_learning.evidence: Student is regularly asked to answer MCQs (turns 1, 11, 13, 29, 42), but tutor sometimes reveals answers directly (turn 44).

direct_instruction_active_practice.evidence: Most teaching segments are followed by a question, but turn 33 adds a diagram explanation then immediately switches topic without practice on that point.

deliberate_practice.evidence: On the arithmetic error at turn 25 (360-190), tutor gave a worked solution but did not offer a similar varied retry; at turn 44 tutor just revealed answer instead of corrective practice.

mastery_learning.evidence: Tutor moved on to supplementary angles (turn 34) and new problems despite repeated arithmetic errors (turns 23, 25, 43); no diagnosis of arithmetic bottleneck.

cognitive_load.evidence: Tutor introduced multiple concepts (angles on a line, vertically opposite, supplementary) in quick succession from turn 20 onward, and turn 33 references a diagram that isn't actually shown.

layering.evidence: Turn 40/41 explicitly links straight-line rule (180°) to the previously mastered point rule (360°).

non_interference.evidence: Confusable rules (around-point 360° vs straight-line 180°) introduced back-to-back at turns 34-38 without explicit discrimination beforehand.

interleaving.evidence: Problem types vary (missing angle, equal-division, straight line, vertically opposite) but variation often arrives before mastery.

testing_effect.evidence: Student attempts retrieval before hints in most turns (e.g., 12, 16, 43), though turn 44 short-circuits retrieval by revealing the answer.

targeted_remediation.evidence: Repeated arithmetic failures (70+120, 360-190) were not remediated with prereq practice on basic addition/subtraction; tutor just supplied the computation.

strongest_behaviors: Consistent use of MCQ retrieval prompts and step-by-step decomposition (e.g., turn 13 splitting the problem into addition then subtraction).
Explicit linking of new rule (straight line = 180°) to mastered rule (around a point = 360°) in turn 41.
weakest_behaviors: Multiple incoherent / contaminated turns where student-role text appears inside tutor turns (turns 7, 19, 28, 40) suggesting role confusion in the orchestration.
Answer reveals and arithmetic bypasses instead of remediation on the genuine bottleneck (basic arithmetic), e.g. turn 44 reveals D) 200° outright.

prompt_recommendations.title: Forbid answer reveal on first error
prompt_recommendations.rationale: At turn 44 the tutor reveals 'The answer is D) 200°' after one wrong attempt, violating mastery and retrieval principles.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add rule: 'Never state the final answer after a single wrong attempt. On error, give one targeted hint or sub-question and require the student to compute the next step themselves. Only reveal after 2+ failed scaffolded attempts.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Forces genuine retrieval and prevents premature answer disclosure.

prompt_recommendations.title: Route arithmetic errors to arithmetic remediation
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Student missed 70+120 (turn 23) and 360-190 (turn 25); tutor explained the geometry rule but never practiced the arithmetic prerequisite.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'If the student's error is arithmetic (not conceptual), pause the geometry sequence and present 2 short arithmetic retrieval items on the same operation before resuming.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Addresses true bottleneck, improves downstream geometry accuracy.

prompt_recommendations.title: Prevent role-confused / contaminated turns
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turns 7, 19, 28, 40 contain text that reads as if the tutor is voicing the student or vice-versa, indicating role bleed.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: You're still not quite there. 270° is like turning to look behind you...
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add explicit role guard: 'Tutor turns must never quote, simulate, or roleplay the student. Output only tutor-voice text. If unsure who is speaking, stop and ask one question.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Eliminates incoherent turns that confuse the student.

prompt_recommendations.title: Make discrimination of confusable rules explicit
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Straight-line (180°) vs around-point (360°) introduced back-to-back without contrastive teaching.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Two straight lines intersect. One angle is 60°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'When introducing a rule that can be confused with one just taught, first present a side-by-side contrast (e.g., 360° around a point vs 180° on a line) with one example of each before practice.'

prompt_recommendations.title: Require inline media or skip the reference
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 33 says 'Looking at this diagram...' but no diagram is rendered for the student.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Looking at this diagram, you can see how four angles around a point add up to 360°.
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Do not reference a diagram or figure unless you have just emitted it via a tool call in the same turn. If no figure is available, describe with words only.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Prevents phantom-media references that erode trust.

prompt_recommendations.title: Mastery gate before introducing new concept
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Tutor jumps to vertically opposite angles (turn 27) and supplementary angles (turn 34) before the student has cleanly solved a missing-angle problem.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's try a different type: Two straight lines intersect. One angle is 60°...
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'Require two consecutive correct independent solves of the current sub-skill before introducing a new sub-skill.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Improves mastery and reduces premature topic switching.

prompt_recommendations.title: Ensure MCQ options match the question stem
prompt_recommendations.rationale: Turn 36 asks which statement is true with text options A-D, but options are labelled 'A) 2 B) 1 C) 3 D) 4'; turn 39 lists numeric options for a statement question.
prompt_recommendations.evidence_quote: Which statement is correct about angles? A) 180 B) 90 C) 360 D) 270
prompt_recommendations.suggested_prompt_edit: Add: 'MCQ answer choices must be the literal candidate answers to the stem. Never present numeric options for a statement-selection question, or vice versa.'
prompt_recommendations.expected_effect: Removes a major source of student confusion and wrong answers.

flow_recommendations.title: Add a coherence/role validator before emitting tutor turn
flow_recommendations.rationale: Several turns flagged 'tutor_incoherent' or 'regen_did_not_clean' show the engine emitting contaminated text.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Suppresses or regenerates turns that contain student-voice fragments or contradictory arithmetic.

flow_recommendations.title: Retry policy that routes to prereq after 2 failures
flow_recommendations.rationale: Engine kept re-asking same-type problems after arithmetic errors; no prereq routing triggered.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: it's c) 180° -> tutor: Not quite. Let's work through 360° - 190° carefully.
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Triggers arithmetic mini-drill instead of repeating the same composite problem.

flow_recommendations.title: Exit-ticket gating between sub-skills
flow_recommendations.rationale: Concepts switched (vertically opposite, supplementary) without a mastery check on the prior skill.
flow_recommendations.evidence_quote: Let's try a different concept: On a straight line, angle A is 120°...
flow_recommendations.expected_effect: Ensures progression only after demonstrated mastery.

experience_recommendations.title: Acknowledge partial progress in error feedback
experience_recommendations.rationale: Repeated 'Not quite' without warm acknowledgement may discourage an error-prone student.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Not quite. Let's work through 360° - 190° carefully.
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Maintains motivation for an error-prone learner.

experience_recommendations.title: Render diagrams when referenced
experience_recommendations.rationale: Student is told to look at a diagram that isn't shown.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Looking at this diagram, you can see how four angles around a point...
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Avoids confusion and builds trust in instructions.

experience_recommendations.title: Slow pacing on rule transitions
experience_recommendations.rationale: Several new concepts appeared in rapid succession, likely overwhelming an error-prone S3 student.
experience_recommendations.evidence_quote: Two straight lines intersect. One angle is 60°. What is the vertically opposite angle?
experience_recommendations.expected_effect: Improves comprehension and reduces error rate.

overall_summary: The session covers the target rule (angles around a point = 360°) and does use retrieval-style MCQs, but is undermined by orchestration bugs (role-confused tutor turns, mismatched MCQ options, phantom diagram), premature answer reveal at turn 44, and a failure to remediate the student's real bottleneck — basic arithmetic. Mastery gating and confusable-concept discrimination are weak. Fixing the role-guard, answer-reveal, and arithmetic-routing rules in the system prompt would yield the largest gains.
